summary: Revision 2026-07-28 makes MCP a stateless, per-request-negotiated protocol over JSON-RPC 2.0. Every request MUST carry `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion"]` (string) and `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities"]` (ClientCapabilities); `clientInfo` (Implementation) and `logLevel` (LoggingLevel) are optional; missing required fields -> `-32602` and HTTP 400. Servers MUST NOT infer capabilities/version/identity from earlier requests on the same connection; cross-request state MUST be referenced by an explicit client-passed identifier. Requests need a non-null string|integer `id` unique among in-flight requests of the sender; notifications have no id and get no response. Every result MUST include `resultType` ("complete" | "input_required" | extension-defined values advertised via capabilities); unknown values are invalid; absent (legacy server) = "complete". Servers SHOULD add `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo"]` to every result. Error codes: standard JSON-RPC (-32700, -32600..-32603); `-32000..-32019` legacy (no new allocation, no assumed meaning except -32002 accepted from legacy servers); `-32020..-32099` spec-only: `-32020` HeaderMismatch, `-32021` MissingRequiredClientCapability (data.requiredCapabilities), `-32022` UnsupportedProtocolVersion (data.supported[], data.requested); each MUST be HTTP 400. `-32002` and `-32042` MUST NOT be emitted. `_meta` key grammar: optional reverse-DNS prefix ending in `/` (second label `modelcontextprotocol` or `mcp` reserved), name `[A-Za-z0-9]` at ends with `-_.` inside; reserved keys: progressToken, protocolVersion, clientInfo, clientCapabilities, logLevel, subscriptionId, serverInfo, traceparent/tracestate/baggage (W3C formats). Subscription-stream notifications MUST carry `subscriptionId`. JSON Schema: default 2020-12, MUST support it, `$schema` may override, unsupported dialect -> error, never auto-fetch network `$ref`, SHOULD bound composition depth. Icons: `src` required (https or data: only), MUST render png/jpeg, SHOULD svg/webp, fetch without credentials, verify magic bytes.

methods.name: <any JSON-RPC request> (generic shape)
methods.params: jsonrpc: "2.0" (required, JSONRPC_VERSION); id: string | number (required; MUST NOT be null; MUST NOT collide with any other in-flight request id of the same sender); method: string (required); params?: object; params._meta: RequestMetaObject (REQUIRED per schema.ts RequestParams line 179-181, because it must hold the two required keys) with: "io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion": string (required); "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities": ClientCapabilities (required; {} = no optional capabilities); "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo"?: Implementation; "io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel"?: LoggingLevel (deprecated as of 2026-07-28, SEP-2577, retained >=12 months); progressToken?: string | number; plus any other keys obeying the _meta grammar. Optional MRTR fields on any client request (schema.ts InputResponseRequestParams 600-609): inputResponses?: InputResponses, requestState?: string.
methods.result: JSONRPCResultResponse: jsonrpc: "2.0"; id: RequestId (same as request); result: Result where result.resultType: ResultType (REQUIRED for 2026-07-28 servers; "complete" | "input_required" | extension string), result._meta?: ResultMetaObject with "io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo"?: Implementation, plus [key: string]: unknown. EmptyResult = Result (only resultType/_meta). PaginatedResult adds nextCursor?: string. CacheableResult adds ttlMs: number (>=0, required on cacheable results) and cacheScope: "public" | "private" (required). InputRequiredResult (resultType "input_required") has inputRequests?: {[key]: CreateMessageRequest|ListRootsRequest|ElicitRequest}, requestState?: string; at least one MUST be present. OR JSONRPCErrorResponse: jsonrpc; id?: RequestId (omitted only when id unreadable due to malformed request); error: {code: integer (required), message: string (required, SHOULD be one concise sentence), data?: unknown}.
methods.capability_gate: None for the envelope. Server MUST NOT use a client capability not present in _meta clientCapabilities of THIS request (else -32021). Method gated behind an undeclared SERVER capability -> -32601 (schema.ts MethodNotFoundError 343-359). resultType values from extensions valid only when that extension is advertised via capabilities.
methods.notes: basic__index.md 'Messages' + 'General fields: _meta'. On HTTP the protocolVersion _meta value MUST match the MCP-Protocol-Version header else 400 (schema.ts RequestMetaObject 69-76; HeaderMismatch -32020). Client MUST treat any unrecognized resultType as invalid; MUST treat absent resultType as "complete" (legacy servers).

methods.name: <any JSON-RPC notification> (generic shape)
methods.params: jsonrpc: "2.0"; method: string; params?: object; params._meta?: NotificationMetaObject with "io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId"?: RequestId (MUST be present on every notification delivered via a subscriptions/listen stream; value = JSON-RPC id of the subscriptions/listen request; absent otherwise, e.g. progress notifications for an in-flight request). MUST NOT include an id.
methods.result: None. Receiver MUST NOT send a response.

methods.name: server/discover
methods.params: params: RequestParams (only _meta with the required per-request fields).
methods.result: DiscoverResult extends CacheableResult: supportedVersions: string[] (required); capabilities: ServerCapabilities (required); instructions?: string; ttlMs: number; cacheScope: "public"|"private"; resultType; _meta.
methods.capability_gate: Servers MUST implement server/discover; clients MAY call it (schema.ts 653-668). No capability required.
methods.notes: Referenced by architecture__index.md 'Capability Negotiation' as the up-front discovery mechanism; full normative text on the server/discover page (not in focus set). ServerCapabilities fields (schema.ts 793-883): experimental?, logging? (deprecated), completions?, prompts?{listChanged?}, resources?{subscribe?,listChanged?}, tools?{listChanged?}, extensions?{[id]: JSONObject}. ClientCapabilities (716-786): experimental?, roots? (deprecated), sampling?{context?,tools?} (deprecated), elicitation?{form?,url?}, extensions?{[id]: JSONObject}. extensions keys MUST follow _meta key grammar with mandatory prefix.

methods.name: subscriptions/listen (envelope aspects only)
methods.params: See subscriptions page (not in focus). Envelope: ordinary request; its JSON-RPC id becomes the subscriptionId.
methods.result: SubscriptionsListenResult: resultType; _meta: SubscriptionsListenResultMetaObject with REQUIRED "io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId": RequestId (equals response id); body otherwise empty. Sent only on graceful teardown.
methods.notes: basic__index.md 'Statelessness': long-lived requests remain request/response; state scoped to the request, not the connection. schema.ts 1320-1352.

methods.name: notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged
methods.params: notifications: SubscriptionFilter (subset of requested types server will honor); _meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId"] REQUIRED (first message carrying that id).
methods.notes: Architecture page sequence diagram; schema.ts 1370-1400. Server MUST NOT send any notification on the subscription before this ack; ordering defined per subscription id, not per channel (stdio may interleave).

methods.name: notifications/progress
methods.params: progressToken: string|number (required, echoes request _meta.progressToken); progress: number (required); total?: number; message?: string.
methods.capability_gate: Opt-in via request _meta.progressToken; receiver not obligated to send.
methods.notes: Reserved _meta key progressToken defined in basic__index.md table; schema.ts 1009-1043. Details on progress page (not in focus).

methods.name: notifications/cancelled
methods.direction: notification c->s (s->c only on stdio to end a subscriptions/listen stream)
methods.params: requestId: RequestId (required; MUST correspond to a request the client previously issued); reason?: string.
methods.notes: schema.ts 620-651: server MUST NOT use it to cancel any request other than a subscriptions/listen stream. Details on cancellation page (not in focus).

requirements.text: All implementations MUST support the base protocol, versioning, and the message patterns; other components MAY be implemented.
All messages MUST follow JSON-RPC 2.0.
Requests MUST include a string or integer ID; the ID MUST NOT be null.
A request ID MUST NOT match the ID of any other request the sender has issued and not yet received a response for.
Result responses MUST include the same ID as the request and MUST include a `result` field; `result` MAY be any JSON object structure.
Every `result` MUST include a `resultType` field (servers implementing 2026-07-28).
The set of supported ResultType values MUST be created from the core set ("complete", "input_required") plus values of supported extensions advertised via capabilities; extensions MAY add values.
A resultType value unrecognized by the client MUST be considered invalid.
Clients MUST treat an absent `resultType` (server on earlier protocol version) as "complete".

Error responses MUST include the same ID as the request (except when the ID could not be read from a malformed request); MUST include `error` with `code` and `message`; codes MUST be integers; MAY include `data` of any type.
Error `message` SHOULD be limited to a concise single sentence.

New error codes MUST NOT be allocated in -32000..-32019; new implementations SHOULD NOT use codes from that sub-range at all; receivers MUST NOT assume any specific meaning for them (apart from -32002).
Implementations MUST NOT emit any code in -32020..-32099 not defined by the spec, and MUST use defined codes only with their specified meanings.
Implementations of 2026-07-28 MUST NOT emit -32002 (resource not found; replaced by -32602) or -32042 (URL elicitation required).
Clients SHOULD still accept -32002 from servers implementing earlier versions.
New non-spec error codes SHOULD be allocated outside the JSON-RPC reserved range -32768..-32000.
Local-only errors surfaced in JSON-RPC-shaped structures (e.g. SDK request timeout) should be distinguishable from peer errors; no spec code is assigned to them.
Receiver of a notification MUST NOT send a response; notifications MUST NOT include an ID.
Servers MUST NOT rely on prior requests over the same connection to establish context (capabilities, protocol version, client identity); every request supplies this in `_meta`.
Servers SHOULD be prepared to handle requests associated with multiple tasks, threads, or conversations.
Servers SHOULD NOT require that a client reuse the same connection or process for related operations.
Clients SHOULD NOT use an individual task, thread, or conversation as the lifetime boundary for the stdio process.
State spanning multiple requests (long-running tasks, application handles) MUST be referenced by an explicit identifier the client passes on each request.

HTTP-transport implementations SHOULD conform to the Authorization spec; STDIO implementations SHOULD NOT follow it and instead retrieve credentials from the environment; custom auth strategies MAY be negotiated.

Clients and servers MUST support JSON Schema 2020-12 for schemas without `$schema`; schemas MAY specify another dialect via `$schema`; implementations MUST support at least 2020-12 and SHOULD document other supported dialects; 2020-12 is RECOMMENDED.

MUST validate schemas according to their declared or default dialect; MUST handle unsupported dialects gracefully by returning an appropriate error indicating the dialect is not supported; schemas MUST be valid per their dialect.
MUST NOT automatically dereference `$ref` values that resolve to a network URI.

MAY offer an opt-in mode fetching non-local `$ref`s, but it MUST be disabled by default and SHOULD enforce a host allowlist or at minimum reject loopback, link-local and private addresses, apply timeouts and size limits, and log dereferenced URIs.
Schemas failing validation due to an unresolved external `$ref` SHOULD be rejected rather than treated as permissive.
SHOULD apply bounds on composition keywords (anyOf/oneOf/allOf/if-then-else) and $defs: max schema depth, cap on subschema count, or per-validation time budget.
Implementations MUST NOT make assumptions about values at reserved `_meta` keys.

`_meta` key prefix, if present, MUST be dot-separated labels followed by `/`; labels MUST start with a letter and end with a letter or digit, interior letters/digits/hyphens; SHOULD use reverse-DNS; any prefix whose second label is `modelcontextprotocol` or `mcp` is reserved.
`_meta` key name, unless empty, MUST begin and end with `[a-z0-9A-Z]`; MAY contain `-`, `_`, `.` and alphanumerics in between.
Every client request MUST include `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion"]` (string) and `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities"]` (ClientCapabilities).
A request missing any required `_meta` field is malformed; server MUST reject with -32602 Invalid params; on HTTP status MUST be 400 Bad Request.
Clients SHOULD include `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo` on every request unless configured not to.

Server MUST NOT rely on capabilities the client has not declared; if a required capability is missing it MUST return MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError (-32021) with `data.requiredCapabilities` listing the missing ones; HTTP status MUST be 400.

On HTTP, `_meta` protocolVersion MUST match the `MCP-Protocol-Version` header, otherwise the server MUST return 400; if the version is unsupported the server MUST return UnsupportedProtocolVersionError (-32022) with data.supported[] and data.requested; HTTP 400.
HeaderMismatchError (-32020) when HTTP header values do not match body values or required headers are missing/malformed; HTTP status MUST be 400.
Servers SHOULD include `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo"]` (Implementation) in every result unless configured not to.
clientInfo/serverInfo are self-reported and unverified; implementations SHOULD NOT use them to change behavior or for security decisions.
requirements.cite: basic__index.md Note under per-response fields; schema.ts 85-88, 152-155

requirements.text: On notifications delivered via a subscriptions/listen stream, the server MUST include `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId"]`.
If `io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel` is absent from a request, the server MUST NOT send notifications/message for that request.
When present, `traceparent`, `tracestate`, `baggage` in `_meta` MUST follow W3C Trace Context / W3C Baggage formats (exception to the prefix rule).
Clients that render icons MUST support image/png and image/jpeg (and image/jpg); SHOULD support image/svg+xml and image/webp.

Icon consumers MUST take security precautions: treat metadata/bytes as untrusted; ensure URI is https or data:; MUST reject unsafe schemes and redirects (javascript:, file:, ftp:, ws:, local app schemes); disallow scheme changes and cross-origin redirects; be resilient to oversized images/frames (MAY set size limits); fetch without credentials (no cookies/Authorization); verify same origin as server; MAY disallow types or sanitize; validate MIME via magic bytes, reject mismatch/unknown; maintain strict allowlist.

Hosts must obtain explicit user consent before exposing user data to servers and before invoking any tool; must not transmit resource data elsewhere without consent; tool annotations from untrusted servers are untrusted.
Implementors SHOULD build consent/authorization flows, document security implications, implement access controls, follow security best practices, consider privacy.
Implemented server features must be advertised in server capabilities; both parties must respect declared capabilities; tool invocation requires the server to declare tools capability.
Servers MUST implement server/discover; clients MAY call it.
InputRequiredResult MUST contain at least one of inputRequests or requestState; client must treat requestState as opaque.

wire_details: Standard error codes: PARSE_ERROR -32700, INVALID_REQUEST -32600, METHOD_NOT_FOUND -32601, INVALID_PARAMS -32602, INTERNAL_ERROR -32603

MCP error codes: HEADER_MISMATCH -32020 (HeaderMismatchError, no data schema), MISSING_REQUIRED_CLIENT_CAPABILITY -32021 (data.requiredCapabilities: ClientCapabilities), UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION -32022 (data.supported: string[], data.requested: string); each MUST be HTTP 400 Bad Request

Range partition: -32000..-32019 legacy/implementation-defined (never allocate new); -32020..-32099 spec-reserved, allocated sequentially from -32020; retired never-reuse: -32002 (resource not found, now -32602), -32042 (URL elicitation required, 2025-11-25 only)

-32602 usage contexts (schema.ts 361-391): unknown tool/invalid tool args, unknown prompt/missing args, invalid/expired cursor, invalid log level, undeclared elicitation mode, sampling tool-result mix; also missing required _meta fields
-32601 usage: unknown method OR method gated behind an unadvertised server capability (e.g. prompts/list without prompts capability)

Reserved _meta keys: progressToken; io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion; io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo; io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities; io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel; io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId; io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo; traceparent; tracestate; baggage

_meta key grammar regex (derived): prefix `([A-Za-z]([A-Za-z0-9-]*[A-Za-z0-9])?)(\.[A-Za-z]([A-Za-z0-9-]*[A-Za-z0-9])?)*/` optional; name `` (empty) or `[A-Za-z0-9]([A-Za-z0-9._-]*[A-Za-z0-9])?`; reserved if second label == modelcontextprotocol|mcp (e.g. io.modelcontextprotocol/, dev.mcp/, org.modelcontextprotocol.api/, com.mcp.tools/); com.example.mcp/ not reserved
ResultType values: "complete", "input_required"; extension values allowed only when extension advertised
HTTP header referenced: MCP-Protocol-Version (must equal _meta protocolVersion; mismatch -> 400 / -32020)
Implementation: name: string (req), version: string (req), title?, description?, websiteUrl? (uri), icons?: Icon[]
Icon: src: string (uri, https or data: only) required; mimeType?: string; sizes?: string[] ("WxH" e.g. "48x48", or "any"); theme?: "light"|"dark"
Icon MIME types: MUST image/png, image/jpeg, image/jpg; SHOULD image/svg+xml, image/webp
CacheableResult: ttlMs: number (>=0; 0 = immediately stale), cacheScope: "public"|"private" (private caches MUST NOT be shared across authorization contexts)
JSON Schema: default dialect https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema when $schema absent; example explicit dialect "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"

Method names appearing in focus pages: server/discover, subscriptions/listen, notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged, notifications/progress, notifications/cancelled, notifications/message, sampling/createMessage (as InputRequest inside InputRequiredResult), tools/call (example)
sdk_implications: Message model: classes/records for JSONRPCRequest (id string|int, non-null), JSONRPCNotification (no id), JSONRPCResultResponse, JSONRPCErrorResponse (id optional). Serializer must emit `jsonrpc:"2.0"` and reject null ids; parser must classify by presence of id/method/result/error and produce -32600/-32700 for malformed input (with id omitted when unreadable).

Request-id allocator must guarantee uniqueness among the sender's in-flight requests (monotonic counter is sufficient); track pending responses per id, including long-lived subscriptions/listen requests.

Client-side request builder must inject `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion"]` and `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities"]` on EVERY request (never rely on a prior initialize), and by default `clientInfo`; expose an opt-out for clientInfo; optional `logLevel` and `progressToken` injection; validate user-supplied _meta keys against the key grammar and forbid reserved prefixes for non-protocol keys.

Server-side request pipeline must, per request and without connection state: validate presence/type of the two required _meta keys (-32602, HTTP 400), check protocol version support (-32022 with data.supported/requested, HTTP 400), on HTTP compare against MCP-Protocol-Version header (-32020/400), and expose a helper that throws -32021 with data.requiredCapabilities when a handler needs an undeclared client capability. Handler context object must carry the per-request ClientCapabilities, protocol version, clientInfo, logLevel — no session object.

Server result builder must always set `resultType` (default "complete") and, unless configured off, `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo"]`; support InputRequiredResult (resultType "input_required", inputRequests/requestState, at least one present).

Client result parser: map resultType; treat absent as "complete" (legacy); throw on unrecognized value unless it belongs to an extension the client negotiated; surface CacheableResult (ttlMs/cacheScope) and PaginatedResult (nextCursor) fields generically.

Error type hierarchy: McpError with code/message/data; typed constants for -32700,-32600,-32601,-32602,-32603,-32020,-32021,-32022; guard that forbids emitting -32002/-32042 and any undefined -32020..-32099 code; local errors (timeouts, transport failures) must use a distinct class or code outside -32768..-32000 and never masquerade as peer errors; accept -32002 from legacy servers when in dual-era client mode.

Notification dispatch: emit no response; for server-side subscription streams stamp `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId"]` = listen request id on every notification and send notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged first; client must route notifications by subscriptionId.

Statelessness: no in-memory 'session' keyed by connection; any cross-request state (tasks, handles) keyed by explicit identifiers passed in params; stdio server must accept interleaved unrelated requests on one process; stdio client must not spawn one process per conversation.

JSON Schema validation component: 2020-12 validator required (PowerShell has none built-in; SDK needs a bundled/ported validator or an optional dependency); honor `$schema` for other dialects or return a clear 'dialect not supported' error; never fetch network `$ref` by default; optional opt-in fetcher with allowlist/private-address rejection/timeouts/size limits/logging; enforce depth/subschema/time bounds; reject schemas with unresolved external $ref.

Icon handling (client side): Icon/Implementation types; loader that only accepts https:/data: URIs, blocks redirects to other origins or unsafe schemes, fetches without credentials, checks magic bytes against allowlist (png, jpeg mandatory; svg, webp optional), applies size limits.
Implementation info type with name/version required, optional title/description/websiteUrl/icons; used both in outgoing _meta (client) and result _meta (server).

Capability types: ClientCapabilities {experimental, roots(deprecated), sampling{context,tools}(deprecated), elicitation{form,url}, extensions{}} and ServerCapabilities {experimental, logging(deprecated), completions, prompts{listChanged}, resources{subscribe,listChanged}, tools{listChanged}, extensions{}}; extension keys validated with mandatory prefix grammar; server must return -32601 for methods whose capability it did not advertise.
OpenTelemetry pass-through: preserve traceparent/tracestate/baggage keys verbatim on _meta; optional validation of W3C format.
Deprecation tracking: logLevel _meta key, roots/sampling client capabilities and logging server capability are deprecated as of 2026-07-28 (SEP-2577) but must still be supported for >=12 months.
legacy_delta: 2025-11-25 / 2025-06-18: stateful `initialize` / `notifications/initialized` handshake negotiated version and capabilities once per session; 2026-07-28 removes it and requires `_meta` protocolVersion + clientCapabilities on every request (changelog item 2, SEP-2575). Dual-era servers must answer `initialize` with legacy semantics scoped to that stdio process/HTTP session; dual-era clients probe with a modern request and fall back to `initialize` on a non-modern error / 4xx without recognized modern error body (basic__versioning.md 131-180).

`_meta` in 2025-11-25 schema was optional on RequestParams (`_meta?: {progressToken?, [key]: unknown}`); in 2026-07-28 RequestParams._meta is required (RequestMetaObject) because it carries required keys. Notification/Result _meta remain optional (except SubscriptionsListenResult).

`resultType` did not exist before 2026-07-28; clients MUST treat absent as "complete". Legacy servers never send "input_required"; server-initiated requests (sampling/createMessage, elicitation/create, roots/list as JSON-RPC requests s->c) are replaced by MRTR InputRequiredResult (changelog item 7).

Error codes: 2025-11-25 defined URL_ELICITATION_REQUIRED -32042 (URLElicitationRequiredError with data.elicitations) — MUST NOT be emitted in 2026-07-28 but a dual-era client talking to a 2025-11-25 server must recognize it. -32002 resource-not-found used by 2025-11-25 and 2025-06-18 servers is replaced by -32602; clients SHOULD still accept -32002. Codes -32020..-32022 and the range policy are new in 2026-07-28; 2025-11-25 schema comment merely said 'Implementation-specific [-32000,-32099]'.

2025-11-25 reserved `_meta` key `io.modelcontextprotocol/related-task` (tasks) existed; new reserved keys in 2026-07-28: protocolVersion, clientInfo, clientCapabilities, logLevel, subscriptionId, serverInfo, plus formal OpenTelemetry keys (traceparent/tracestate/baggage, changelog minor item 2).

`ping`, `logging/setLevel`, `notifications/roots/list_changed` removed in 2026-07-28 (changelog item 5); log level now via `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel"]`; a dual-era SDK must still implement them for legacy sessions.
Implementation type: 2025-06-18 had no icons (Implementation extends BaseMetadata only); 2025-11-25 added Icon/Icons, description, websiteUrl; 2026-07-28 unchanged in shape.

Server capability discovery moved from InitializeResult (protocolVersion, capabilities, serverInfo, instructions) to `server/discover` DiscoverResult (supportedVersions[], capabilities, instructions, ttlMs, cacheScope); serverInfo now travels in result _meta.
Client capabilities roots and sampling, and server capability logging, are deprecated in 2026-07-28 (SEP-2577) but were first-class in 2025-11-25 / 2025-06-18.

HTTP: 2025-11-25 used MCP-Protocol-Version header plus Mcp-Session-Id sessions; 2026-07-28 keeps MCP-Protocol-Version (must match _meta) and defines HeaderMismatch -32020; session semantics are covered on the transport page (not in this focus set).
open_questions: The basic page says 'error responses MUST include the same ID... except where the ID could not be read'; whether a server may respond with `id: null` (JSON-RPC style) vs omitting `id` is not stated — schema.ts makes `id` optional (omit), no null allowed for requests; SDK should omit.

The 'Required' column marks protocolVersion and clientCapabilities required on 'every request' — whether this applies to legacy `initialize` in dual-era mode is defined on the versioning page, not here.
Exact HTTP error-body expectations for -32602 on missing _meta fields (JSON-RPC error body vs plain 400) are stated only as 'status MUST be 400'; body format presumably per streamable-http page.

Which HTTP status applies when a client receives -32021/-32022 over stdio is moot; over HTTP 400 — but whether the client should retry automatically with a version from data.supported is only 'should choose ... and retry' in schema.ts (non-normative casing).

Whether `_meta` keys with an EMPTY name (grammar allows 'unless empty') are actually usable (e.g. key `io.modelcontextprotocol/`) is unclear; SDK should reject empty names conservatively or allow per grammar — needs decision.
The spec lists icon `mimeType` as advisory and requires magic-byte detection, but provides no normative list beyond png/jpeg/svg/webp; SDK allowlist policy for gif etc. is implementation choice.
The three MCP error codes' `message` texts are not standardized (examples referenced via includeCode not in local material).

Logging `_meta` logLevel is deprecated in schema.ts (SEP-2577) while the basic page still lists it as an active reserved key without deprecation note; the replacement mechanism (if any) is not visible in the focus pages — check logging page / deprecated.md.

No explicit MUST on how a server should handle a request whose `_meta` contains reserved-prefix keys it does not understand (ignore vs reject); only 'MUST NOT make assumptions about values'. SDK should ignore unknown keys.
